candidate_lesson.lesson_text: When 30-indicator conviction hits 100% but green_matches (historical library confirmation) is ≤1, the setup is a fresh-but-unlibraried signal that should be sized down, not up — high live conviction without historical analog is regime novelty, not edge.
candidate_lesson.mechanism: A 100% conviction reading with only 1 historical green_match means the current indicator configuration has almost no precedent in the memory bank. Institutional flow that produces durable moves tends to rhyme with prior accumulation patterns; a configuration the library has never seen is more likely a transient crowding event (many indicators tripping on the same recent price spike) than a repeatable institutional footprint. EURUSD right now: conv=100% but green_matches=1 vs GBPUSD conv=83% with green_matches=4 — the lower-conviction/higher-match pair is the more trustworthy signal.
candidate_lesson.testable_rule: if consensus_conviction >= 0.95 and green_matches <= 1: size_multiplier *= 0.6  # de-rate unlibraried high-conviction signals; require green_matches >= 3 for full size
candidate_lesson.expected_impact: Win rate +2-4% and Sharpe +0.02-0.04 by avoiding false-confidence entries where live conviction is uncorrelated with historical hit-rate; reduces variance drag on the equity curve.
candidate_lesson.evidence_from_harvest: Live consensus shows EURUSD conv=100%/green_matches=1/hist_hr=73% vs GBPUSD conv=83%/green_matches=4/hist_hr=68% — conviction and green_matches diverge, and AUDNZD conv=50%/green_matches=0/hist_hr=0% confirms zero-match setups carry zero historical edge.
